verdict.rationale: Problem in: accuracy, repeats. (Rule inferred from the POC spec and notebook; status-based, scores unused.)

results.summary: 60 of 80 scans (75%) have a near-identical twin; there are only 40 real patients behind 80 scans. 31 of the twins are filed under a different patient ID, so ID-based checks would miss them. Accuracy measured on this data will look better than it really is until repeats are removed. A random split gives 2.6 mm error but the honest by-patient split gives 6.7 mm: the data leaks, so random-split results here are too optimistic.

4 scan(s) where the model's diameter differs from the label by more than 4.2 mm (3x the reference spread). Worth a manual look.
The model caught 6 of 7 aneurysms (sensitivity 86%, plausible range 49% to 97%; reference 89%). Balanced accuracy 0.90, G-mean 0.90.
Diameter error: on average 0.7 mm (reference 0.7 mm); 93% of scans within 2 mm; bias -0.2 mm.
Problem 'many no-answers' in: contrast_phase=arterial (n=16), contrast_phase=non-contrast (n=18), slice_thickness_class=standard (n=38), sex=F (n=34), scanner_vendor=siemens (n=57).
The model's aorta outline overlaps the expert outline well in most scans (median Dice 0.98, reference 0.98); 5% of scans are below 0.90.
Scans with a poor outline (Dice < 0.90) have an average diameter error of 4.9 mm, versus 0.5 mm for the rest.

notes: R2 is unreliable with this few scans and a narrow diameter range; compare errors in mm and the random-vs-patient gap instead.

provenance.source: SlicePoint hackathon POC (notebooks + POC spec), via data-contract-inventory.md
provenance.author: SlicePoint student team; transcribed by slicepoint-schemas
provenance.notes: Reproduces the POC, not a clinical recommendation. Conflicts: (1) min group size is 12-14 in the spec vs n>=15 in the notebook flag_row; the notebook value 15 is used. (2) The spec's Dice UI markers (0.81/0.90) differ from the notebook/monitor Dice thresholds (red 0.85 / yellow 0.90), which are kept in triggers. (3) The spec says population SD; the notebook mixes population and sample SD; slicepoint-core uses population SD (ddof=0) throughout, see core PARITY.md. (4) monitor.py emits the 'Aneurysms the model caught' row with worse='high' when there are fewer than 3 aneurysms (value n/a); the intended direction is low and that is what is stored here. (5) The notebook-specific rules (triggers with snake_case keys and `parameters`) were added for slicepoint-core milestone 1; they are transcribed from test_your_hospital.ipynb and are what the five checks read.

check_descriptors.title: Different people
check_descriptors.definition: Scans per distinct person: guards against repeat scans and patient leakage inflating accuracy. Notebook logic: near-duplicate groups (cosine > 0.95 or same patient_id) and the random vs by-patient split test.

check_descriptors.title: Scan settings match
check_descriptors.definition: Similarity of the acquisition mix to the reference; the card shows the lowest of scanner, contrast and slice thickness. Notebook logic: TVD, HU/kVp/slice Wasserstein, embedding domain AUC, coverage, impossible values.
